paper.title: Don't Just Listen, Try Planning: Graph-based Retrieval-Generation Agent for Long-form Audio Meeting Understanding

latest_version.version_label: ACL Anthology camera-ready (Findings of ACL 2026, pp. 20715-20742), reviewed 2026-08-30

evidence.section: 2 Dataset Construction; 2.2 Question Definition and Data Annotation
evidence.paraphrase: LongAudioQA is built from AliMeeting (14.91 h, 3,013 QA), AMI (18.24 h, 3,243 QA) and concatenated DailyTalk (21.59 h, 10,200 QA), with meetings averaging ~32 minutes and 757-815 turns. Questions span Factual, Inferential (multi-hop, coreference, stance tracking), Temporal (absolute localization, relative sequencing), Summarization and Acoustic-Aware categories; acoustic-aware items are generated so that they cannot be answered from the transcript alone and require emotion/volume grounding at a timestamp.

The benchmark is designed against 'context fragmentation': the generation process uses oracle local evidence, but evaluated systems must recover answers from global long-context meeting data without knowing the relevant segment. Timestamp evidence must reach IoU > 0.9 with ground truth and human verification yields kappa = 0.91.

adjudication_notes: Retained as memory-adjacent: it stresses long-range retention, temporal grounding and cross-modal (acoustic) evidence over ~30-minute meetings, but it evaluates long-form audio QA rather than prescribing or probing a persistent agent-memory architecture.
Separate record from the GRGA architecture per counting rules; both derive from the same paper.
